title: How the ZIA Terraform provider applies rule order

prose.text: The ZIA provider does not write a rule's declared order directly: it hands the declared position to a background worker that moves the rule there. Up to v4.8.13 every update first moved the rule out of the way, and from v4.8.14 only a rank change does. {{update-parks-every-update}} {{list-error-then-panic}} {{parking-spot-from-truncated-list}} {{delete-renumber-same-apply}}

prose.label: Rules the apply did not touch.
prose.text: {{terminal-rule-can-be-displaced}} Product-side rule order semantics are in [[zia.url-filtering.rule-order]].

update-parks-every-update.statement: Up to v4.8.13 every URL Filtering rule update, whatever field changed, was first sent with rank 7 at the order of the last rule (sorted by rank, then order), and only afterwards moved back to its declared order by the reorder worker; the rule was written at that order, not after it. From v4.8.14 an update that changes only `order` writes nothing, an update that changes other attributes but not `rank` is written at the rule's current position, and only an update that changes `rank` is written at the end of the list with rank 7; the declared position is then handed to the reorder engine.

list-error-then-panic.statement: Before v4.8.11, if listing the existing rules failed during an update, the error was only logged and the code read the last element of whatever came back: if the first page failed, the list was empty and the index panicked; if a later page failed, the rule was parked using a partial list. v4.8.11 returns the list error from the update before the index is read (#610). From v4.8.14 the update no longer indexes the last element: the end of the list comes from `endOfList`, which starts at order 1, and the list is read only when `rank` changed, with a failed read returned as an error.
list-error-then-panic.conditions: Changed upstream in v4.8.11 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "If listing the existing rules fails during an update, the error is only logged and the code reads the last element of whatever came back: if the first page failed, the list is empty and the index panics; if a later page failed, the rule is parked using a partial list."

parking-spot-from-truncated-list.statement: The order used to park a rule comes from a list read through the Go SDK's GetAll, which can return a truncated list; up to v4.8.13 on every URL Filtering update, from v4.8.14 only on an update that changes `rank`. With more rules than one page holds, the "highest existing order" can be a position inside the policy rather than its end.

background-worker.statement: Declared orders are applied by one background worker per rule type. It rescans on a 30-second ticker, sleeping for half the interval between checks, and each pass reads current positions once.

worker-cannot-report-failure.statement: The reorder worker has no way to report failure: `reorderAll` returns no value, and waiting resources are released by closing a channel. A reorder that gives up looks like success to Terraform.

unregistered-rules-not-compared.statement: A rule the apply did not register is never compared with a declared position or moved by the worker; it enters a pass only through the read of current positions.
unregistered-rules-not-compared.conditions: Read from reorderAll: the comparison and move loop ranges over the sorted registry, and the read of current positions is used only for lookups and the orderable count.

stale-positions-within-a-pass.statement: Within a pass, each rule is compared against the positions read at the start of the pass; positions are not refreshed after a move, so later rules in the same pass are judged against stale positions.

gives-up-silently.statement: The worker gives up and returns, with no value to report, in several situations: after six ticks in which registered rules stay deferred or their moves fail with no progress, or after two ticks in which only deferred rules remain. From v4.8.7 an oscillation breaker (SUP-4231) also logs the still-misplaced rules and returns after repeated passes that issue PUTs without improving on the best at-target count. From v4.8.11 it also returns after six consecutive passes in which the current rule order could not be read (#610); before v4.8.11 a failed read only logged the error and continued, so a read that kept failing kept the worker looping. The v4.8.11 comment says the waiting create or update then reads the rule back and reports the API error.
gives-up-silently.conditions: Changed upstream in v4.8.11 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "The worker returns without an error in several situations: after six ticks in which registered rules stay deferred or their moves fail with no progress, or after two ticks in which only deferred rules remain. From v4.8.7 an oscillation breaker also returns after repeated non-improving passes (SUP-4231). Waiters proceed as if the order were applied."

[PR #610](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zia/pull/610) - Fixed rule-based resources hanging indefinitely while placing rules in their declared order when the current rule order could not be read from the API. After repeated failed reads the provider now stops waiting and reports the API error.

wrong-order-reported-success.statement: So an apply can finish successfully with rules out of their declared order, and only a later plan's drift shows it.
wrong-order-reported-success.conditions: Chain of evidence: the reorder worker cannot report a failure, gives up without an error and converges on registered rules only (the claims derived from). Not observed on a tenant.

terminal-rule-can-be-displaced.statement: Up to v4.8.13, editing any field of a rule placed above a terminal deny could leave the deny no longer last: the edit parked the rule below it, and if moving it back failed or gave up, the apply still reported success. From v4.8.14 only an edit that changes `rank` parks the rule at the end of the list.
terminal-rule-can-be-displaced.conditions: Depends on how the API renumbers the other rules when one is written at a given order, and on the API accepting a write at the last rule's order even when that is a predefined default rule (gap api-order-shift); on the edited rule not already being last and the terminal rule being at or near the end; and on the move back failing or giving up. For v4.8.14 the parking is only on a rank change (claim update-parks-every-update), so the exposure is narrower; the chain beyond that is unchanged.

delete-renumber-same-apply.statement: Before v4.8.14, deleting a rule and changing the order of the remaining rules in one apply could fail with `INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT` `Rule is not allowed at order N`, and the documentation advised deleting the rule with `-target` first. v4.8.14 fixed this: a rule whose only change is `order` is no longer rewritten, and a write the API rejects because the rule list changed is retried, at most three times.

api-order-shift.title: How the ZIA API renumbers other rules when a rule is written at a given order
api-order-shift.blocks: stating exactly where a parked rule lands and which neighbors move
api-order-shift.detail: The provider assumes ordered-list behavior (the written rule takes the position and the rest shift). No captured source states the API's renumbering rule, or whether it rejects a write at a predefined default rule's order. Test in a scratch tenant by writing a rule at a lower order, and at the default rule's order, and re-reading every rule's order.
